g.text: to foundation models you call as a service
2017 — VASWANI ET AL., "ATTENTION IS ALL YOU NEED"

div.style: font-size:23px; line-height:1.45; color:#1f1a14; font-style:italic; font-family:Georgia, serif;

foreignObject.div: For most of AI's history the bottleneck was the model — every task needed its own data, pipeline, and training run. The Transformer removed the architectural ceiling on long text, and five years of scaling turned the result into foundation models you call from a one-line API. The new job is not training models; it is architecting systems of agents around them.

Note the lecturer's date for the perceptron is off by two years. 1956 = Dartmouth workshop (the name "Artificial Intelligence" was coined); 1958 = Rosenblatt's perceptron paper. Different events, separated by two years.

g.text: 1. Pick foundation model · API or weights
Process tokens one at a time.
Every token attends to every other.
Parallel on GPU. O(n²) attention cost.
Five families — one dominates production today

foreignObject.div: * The slide labels RNN as a generative model — shorthand for RNN language models (char-RNN, ELMo-style). RNNs the architecture aren't inherently generative; only when wired as next-token predictors. Almost entirely displaced by Transformers. Diffusion (added in the bottom row, not on the slide) is the 2026-relevant family for image/video generation.
